subject: kimi-code
title: Composable first-match permission policy chain evaluated in the executor's before-tool hook
one_why: 13 named policies (user deny/ask/allow, dangerous-command, sensitive-file, git-path, session-history, yolo, fallback-ask) resolve in explicit constructor order, each emitting telemetry with the winning policy name; easy to adopt wholesale and far more debuggable than one monolithic canUseTool.

subject: kimi-code
title: Dangerous-command detection over a tree-sitter-bash AST, not regex
one_why: Inverts the corpus's regex-denylist anti-pattern: parses the command via a real grammar with nested-shell depth cap (4), unsafe-operand bail-out, and sudo/doas wrapper unwrapping before deciding ask; the grammar ships as its own package with tests.

subject: kimi-code
title: No OS-level sandbox: approved tools execute with full user privileges
evidence: repo-wide grep for seatbelt/sandbox-exec/bwrap/landlock/seccomp in src: zero hits (only pi-tui/src/terminal.ts false positive)
one_why: Approval is the entire enforcement story; a prompt-injected but approved command, or any allow-rule hit, runs unconfined - codex-tier safety needs a kernel layer under this otherwise strong gate.

subject: kimi-code
title: Dangerous-command guard silently dropped in non-interactive mode
one_why: bootstrap.args.nonInteractive splices DangerousCommandAsk out of the chain, so headless runs where the user configured allow-rules lose the extra dangerous-command check with no deny/fallback of its own (mitigated somewhat by fallback-ask and the --prompt/--yolo conflict, cli/options.ts:79-80).

subject: kimi-code
title: Graduated repeat breaker: reminders at streak 3/5/8, hard force-stop at 12
one_why: Stronger than crush's binary breaker: escalating in-result reminders then a terminal force-stop result that refuses further tool calls for the step, with dedup of identical parallel calls in the same step folded into the same streak accounting.

subject: kimi-code
title: Agent state is a replayable event fold with undoable keys and journal repair migrations
one_why: Session resume, conversation undo, and permission-mode history all fall out of one replayable/undoable state model over a repairable wire journal - the deepest state model in the corpus after codex's rollout journals, and tested across migrations.

subject: kimi-code
title: Fork governance: UPSTREAM.md intent cards pin the vendor delta against a fixed upstream commit
evidence: packages/pi-tui/UPSTREAM.md:1-60 (Last Sync Point 53816d7dcc5ebe3a0eedec3cd07196c3a66d83fd + keep/absorbed intent cards)
one_why: A reusable recipe for carrying a vendored upstream library: every local behavior change must map to an intent card that says why it cannot live in the app, and the fork must reconstruct cleanly against the pinned upstream ref - worth copying for any vendor decision, license-independent.

subject: kimi-code
title: minidb: pure-Node embedded KV store (WAL group-commit, skip-list indexes, torn-tail truncation) backing agent persistence
evidence: packages/minidb/README.md:8-30; packages/minidb/src/mini-db.ts (1470 LOC); test coverage 15k LOC
one_why: Zero-native-addons durable store (Redis AOF policies + SQLite WAL ideas) so sessions/tasks survive crashes without shipping sqlite natives; crash-torn tails are CRC-detected and truncated on recovery.

subject: kimi-code
title: AGENTS.md late-reminder and instruction drift injection
one_why: Instead of eagerly stuffing every nested AGENTS.md into the prompt, kimi detects instruction files applying to paths a tool call just touched and queues a reminder - and re-flags files that changed on disk after injection; solves both token economy and stale-instruction correctness.

subject: kimi-code
title: btw: side-question agent on a lightweight instance, read-only tools, tool defs kept visible to preserve prompt cache
one_why: Users can ask side questions without interrupting the running turn; disabled tool definitions are deliberately retained in the request because removing them would break the provider prompt cache - explicit cache-aware prompt construction, rare in the corpus.

subject: kimi-code
title: Scripted streaming provider harness drives loop, compaction, and permission tests
one_why: A fake generate() that emits real stream part sequences (text/think/tool_call_part with stream indices) lets ~16.7k tests exercise full turn semantics offline across the whole monorepo - the strongest faux-provider corpus found after codex's mock SSE suites.

subject: kimi-code
title: 357k LOC of tests and 9 workflows, but zero model evals or fuzz targets
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-160 (build/smoke, 5-shard vitest, lint, tsgo; grep 'eval' across workflows: no matches); Windows matrix disabled at :93
one_why: Shares the corpus-wide verification ceiling: nothing measures model-behavior quality (compaction fidelity, loop-breaker effectiveness against real trajectories), so model/prompt regressions ship silently.
